ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against Colombian Procuraduría General de la Nación, Contraloría General de la República, UIAF official PEP lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Interpol Red Notices; enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP or family member/close associate; ongoing transaction monitoring under Circular Externa 002 de 2022; reporting of suspicious transactions within 6 days of detection to UIAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via the Cámara de Comercio online portal (www.rue.com.co) and the Official Bulletin of the Chamber of Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish or include Spanish transliteration; names may include Latin script; use of English words is permissible only as part of a coined expression if transliterated or directly adapted to Spanish phonetics; the prefix or suffix 'S.A.S.' must appear; names must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name; reserved names are checked by the Chamber of Commerce against the national registry index.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 5 business days of the rejection notice, the applicant must file a written reconsideration request with the local Chamber of Commerce Appeals Committee, attaching the original name clearance receipt and evidence of the proposed name's distinctiveness; if denied at the Chamber level, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición y en subsidio apelación) before the Chamber's Legal Director and then the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within 10 business days; whenever a name is rejected on grounds of prohibitive token usage, a ministerial prior authorization must be obtained from the relevant Ministry (e.g., Ministry of Finance for 'Banco' or 'Seguros') before resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office use is highly restricted for an esports community platform because the entity must maintain a physical registered address in Colombia where the legal representative and accounting records are effectively located; however, a service provider virtual office may be used as the registered address only if it provides physical reception of legal notices, access to corporate books, and a dedicated meeting space, and if the company's actual operational management remains conducted through Colombian-based outsourced staff; purely mailbox-type virtual offices without local staff presence are not acceptable for DIAN tax registration or Chamber of Commerce inspection compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Arts. 1, 2, 5, 9, 11, 17 and 45; Código de Comercio de Colombia (Decreto 410 de 1971), Arts. 98, 110 and 354; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Book 2, Title 1, Chapter 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) acting through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES); oversight by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento privado de constitución (private deed of incorporation) containing the estatutos, registered with the Registro Mercantil of the relevant Chamber of Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-in capital is required for an S.A.S.; capital may be expressed in Colombian pesos or foreign currency, and bylaw payment terms may extend up to two years from incorporation per Article 9 of Ley 1258; no escrow account or bank capital deposit certificate is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. — By unanimous written consent of the shareholders, the Board resolves: (1) The subscribed capital stated in the bylaws is ratified and each subscriber is bound to contribute per the payment schedule established under Article 9 of Law 1258 of 2008; (2) The registered office is established at [address], [city], Colombia, and the incorporation deed shall be filed with the Chamber of Commerce; (3) [Name] is appointed Legal Representative and [Name] Alternate Legal Representative, with full powers of representation and execution as set forth in the bylaws, effective immediately; (4) The Legal Representative is instructed to procure the RUT, open bank accounts, and perform all ancillary registrations. Approved, signed, and recorded this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social through the RUES online portal (www.rues.org.co) or in-person service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names through the RUES homonym search module; pay the nominal search fee; obtain the certificate of homonymy (certificado de homonimia), which remains valid for 90 calendar days; no notarization is required for the S.A.S. private-deed route.
required_dossiers: RUES name-search application form
Valid government-issued identity card of the applicant
Proposed corporate names list (up to three)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File additional name variants at no further substantive cost, or submit a motion for review (recurso de reposición) before the same Chamber within 5 business days; if the name is found identical, substitute a new distinctive corporate denomination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Private Incorporation Deed and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All founding shareholders (constituents); optional Notaría if a public deed is preferred
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the estatutos containing corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose, capital structure, share classes and voting rights, board structure (administrador único or multiple officers), governance rules, and duration; execute the document privately with all shareholders' signatures; no paid-in capital deposit or escrow is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Draft private incorporation deed and bylaws
Identity documents of each shareholder
Certificate of homonymy
Valid contact e-mail and telephones of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defect or omission is cured by an additional corrective private document (documento aclaratorio) executed by the same shareholders and attached to the deed before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Issuance of Existence Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (online virtual office or physical window); registry database maintained under RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed deed together with the standardized registration form (Formulario de Registro y Matrícula Mercantil); pay the registration and mercantile registration fees calculated on the declared capital; the Chamber verifies legal compliance and, upon approval, issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation deed and bylaws
Formulario de Registro y Matrícula Mercantil
Certificate of homonymy
Shareholder identity documents
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice (requerimiento) is issued, correct the observations within the term indicated by the Chamber or file the corrective document; if registration is refused, appeal to the Superintendencia de Sociedades within 10 business days with the full record of the request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) through the MUISCA online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the integrated RUES/DIAN registration to obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria); assign the CIIU code 5820 for software publishing and the e-sports platform as the economic activity; declare the ordinary or simple taxation regime; the RUT is generally generated on the same day or within the following business day.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Identity card of the legal representative
Extract of bylaws reflecting the legal representative's appointment
Lease agreement or sworn declaration of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or queries the form, amend the data online through MUISCA; unresolved discrepancies may be corrected in person at the assigned DIAN office with original supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Ancillary Municipal/Occupational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any supervised credit institution; municipal Alcaldía (industry and commerce tax - ICA); Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name with the legal representative's credentials; register the company for the municipal industry and commerce tax if a physical presence is established; affiliate the legal representative and employees with an ARL and enroll payroll in the integrated social security system.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (no older than 90 days)
RUT
Bylaws
Identity card of the legal representative
Bank account application forms
Lease agreement or proof of establishment address (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines account opening, resubmit with refined corporate compliance documentation or approach another supervised credit institution; municipal ICA registration gaps may be cured by filing the current year's ICA declaration with the local tax administration, subject to applicable interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Tecnologías de la Información y las Comunicaciones (MinTIC) — ICT services are regulated but the operation of an e-sports software platform requires no manufacturing or industrial permit; general telecom/ICT registration remains voluntary for this activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating or manufacturing license is triggered for ISIC 5820 software publishing; optional confidentiality and data-processing registrations may be made under Ley 1581 de 2012 for personal data handling.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the regional Corporaciones Autónomas Regionales (CAR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is purely digital with no physical transformation of inputs; no EIA or environmental registration is required for the virtual platform, and at most a declaration of negligible impact is needed should an office be occupied.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or industrial emission thresholds apply to pure software operation; if servers or office equipment are later deployed, disposal of waste electrical and electronic equipment (RAEE) must follow Resolución 1407 de 2011, and general sanitation standards under Decreto 1076 de 2015 must be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for virtual-only operations; if a physical office is leased, the company must obtain the municipal certificate of land use (uso de suelo), a fire-safety approval from the local Cuerpo de Bomberos, and comply with workplace safety registration under Resolución 0312 de 2019 through the affiliated ARL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Colombia's national tax and customs authority. Official portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; MUISCA e-services portal (RUT registration, NIT management, VAT filing): https://muisca.dian.gov.co; foreign-trade single window (VUCE/SIEX): https://vuce.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The S.A.S., even if 100% non-resident owned, is a Colombian domestic entity and must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), which serves simultaneously as the income-tax ID and the IVA/VAT registration number. Procedure: (1) execute the S.A.S. bylaws before a Colombian notary, register with the Cámara de Comercio, and appoint a legal representative domiciled in Colombia; (2) apostille or legalize all foreign corporate documents and supply official Spanish translations; (3) file Form 50 (Registro Único Tributario, RUT) via DIAN's pre-registration web module or at the DIAN office, stating ISIC/CIIU 5820 (software publishing / sporting platforms) and the obligation to invoice with IVA; (4) upon approval, DIAN assigns the NIT and generates the RUT certificate; (5) update the RUT to add the export-service status ('exportador de servicios') and, if desired, the SIMPLE-regime election; (6) obtain a DIAN-authorized electronic signature (firma electrónica) through a certified certificate authority for MUISCA and e-invoicing access. Payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal) and Colombian banks will require the NIT/RUT as part of account onboarding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Colombian S.A.S. is a resident juridical entity taxed at the entity level on worldwide net income (35% corporate rate for 2025); there is no pass-through eligibility. Income derived from the esports platform is ordinary business income subject to full assessment, while certain passive foreign-source income may qualify for territorial-reach exemptions. Shareholders bear additional dividend and/or remittance taxation at the beneficiary level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no check-the-box election; entity-level taxation is non-electively mandatory. The material elections and special-rule mechanisms available to an S.A.S. engaged in software/esports exports are: (i) the optional Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) for qualifying small taxpayers whose prior-year gross income does not exceed COP 3,500 million, which consolidates income and IVA remittance mechanics; (ii) the ZOMAC reduced-rate election for new companies located in conflict-affected municipalities (subject to its statutory eligibility window); (iii) the 'economía naranja' enhanced deduction for software and creative-industry investment where the statutory conditions are met; (iv) export-service IVA zero-rating classification declared in the RUT and applied through the FEV; and (v) anti-hybrid mismatch rules under Colombian law that, without any election, deny or defer deductions or tax credits to the extent that hybrid instruments or hybrid entities produce a mismatch in the counterparty's jurisdiction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia) as the monetary and foreign-exchange authority; Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia as the financial supervisor and licensing authority for authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries; Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) as the customs and tax authority for merchandise trade declarations and underlying export/import operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a single free-floating exchange market rather than a fixed-rate system. The Colombian peso is generally convertible for current-account transactions and for capital-account transactions, provided the funds are channeled through an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary and properly reported under the national exchange regime. Capital-account transactions, including equity contributions, foreign loans, and foreign direct investment, are subject to registration requirements with Banco de la República. Profit remittance by a Colombian S.A.S. is legally permissible after compliance with corporate and tax obligations, including audited financial statements where required and distribution minutes adopted by the shareholders; remittances must be made through an authorized intermediary and supported by the underlying international investment registration. Colombia does not impose multiple exchange rates, quantitative exchange rationing, or prior exchange-license requirements for ordinary trade and investment remittances, but the use of non-channelized offshore balances violates the foreign-exchange regime and may trigger DIAN sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods exporters must channel 100% of their export proceeds through the authorized Colombian foreign-exchange market within six (6) calendar months following the date of the export customs declaration (DEX). Exporters of software and cross-border digital services must channel service-proceeds within six (6) months from the date the income is accrued or invoiced under the applicable service contract, unless a longer term is authorized by the foreign-exchange regime. The statutory mandatory channeling ratio is 100%: the foreign currency must be sold to an authorized intermediary, deposited into a Colombian foreign-currency account, or used for permitted external obligations through an authorized intermediary. There is no separate legal obligation to convert into Colombian pesos if the exporter elects to maintain a foreign-currency account. Revenue collected by offshore payment processors such as Stripe or PayPal is not exempt and must ultimately be repatriated into the Colombian treasury account and reported through the applicable Declaración de Cambio.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium as a primary treasury rail; Medium as an ancillary collection-only facility. Offshore digital EMI entities are not recognized as authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries under the Colombian exchange regime and therefore cannot legally serve as the sole channel for the S.A.S.'s export proceeds, foreign investment capital, or FX payments. Colombian law permits specialized electronic deposit and payment institutions, known as SEDPEs, to operate payment services under the supervision of Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, but an offshore EMI must either partner with such a licensed local institution or use a local commercial bank clearing agreement to collect and deposit funds in Colombia. A Colombian S.A.S. may maintain ancillary accounts at foreign EMIs for e-commerce convenience, but those accounts must be transparently connected to the local treasury and the funds must be channelized into Colombia according to the mandatory surrender rules. Direct use of an unlicensed foreign EMI as the main operational account creates a legal red flag under AML/KYC and foreign-exchange compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Colombian S.A.S. opening a corporate bank account must nominate a legal representative with verified identity. For domestic directors and local legal representatives, physical presence is normally required at the bank branch or a certified notary to execute account-opening documents and specimen signatures. Fully remote corporate account opening is not a statutory entitlement in Colombia and is generally only accepted for low-risk companies when the bank has an approved digital onboarding tool with a video-KYC interview. Non-resident directors or shareholders must have their documents notarized, apostilled or legally recognized by Colombian consular rules, and their powers of attorney registered with the Cámara de Comercio where necessary. It is advisable, and in most bank compliance policies required, that the local legal representative or principal shareholder attend an in-person or interactive video KYC interview before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners with no Colombian tax residence, no local physical office, and no verifiable source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled/notarized passports of all UBOs; Colombian RUT and NIT certificate for the S.A.S.; certified copy of the Cámara de Comercio registration; certificate of existence and legal representation; executed shareholder subscription agreement; bank reference letters from foreign banks; formal statement of source of funds and source of wealth; corporate group organigram; business plan evidencing real commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity inbound digital payments from Stripe, PayPal, and other payment aggregators into a newly formed software/esports platform in the initial account opening period.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete merchant agreements with Stripe and PayPal; merchant settlement reports; verified identity and KYC records of platform users; detailed tournament rules and matchmaking policies; prize disbursement schedules; refund and chargeback policy; geolocation and fraud-detection procedures; auditable transaction reconciliation framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to international tournament winners and foreign players may be mischaracterized by the bank as gambling/lottery proceeds, unlicensed betting, or prize-money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Colombian legal opinion confirming that the esports community platform is a skill-based tournament and matchmaking business, not a betting or gambling site; platform terms of service; absence of wagering mechanics; no odds or casino-game functionality; AML screening of all prize recipients; sanctions-list and OFAC screening; cumulative prize thresholds; tax withholding certificates where required by Colombian tax law; signed player attestations of fair play and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly incorporated S.A.S. with minimal paid-in capital but immediately projected high gross revenue from cross-border tournament operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized bylaws of the S.A.S.; paid-in capital bank certificate; sworn capital contribution minutes; Cámara de Comercio certificate of incorporation; audited or CPA-reviewed pro-forma financial statements; board-approved cash-flow budget; capitalization table; shareholder loan agreements if applicable; investor pipeline and sponsorship agreements; enterprise software licenses and hosting contracts evidencing digital infrastructure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity capital must be transferred from the non-resident investor's bank by SWIFT MT103 to the S.A.S.'s designated capital-receiving account at an authorized Colombian bank. The wire must uniquely identify the beneficiary S.A.S. NIT and the investor legal entity, and the payment purpose code in the SWIFT field 50/59 or remittance information must clearly indicate Foreign Direct Investment - Equity Capital Injection. The receiving authorized financial intermediary is required to prepare and file the applicable Declaración de Cambio for international investment on, or immediately after, the transaction date. The investor or the S.A.S. must subsequently register the investment in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales of Banco de la República under the applicable rules, and the assigned file number must be maintained for all future dividend repatriation and capital-disinvestment transactions. Equity funds may not be routed through an unregulated offshore EMI or crypto-fiat conduit as a substitute for this channelized banking route. If the S.A.S. uses a foreign currency account, the capital declaration will reflect the maintained foreign-currency position, while any local operational funding requires conversion into COP at a free-market rate negotiated with the authorized intermediary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade flows should be cleared through the Colombian S.A.S.'s operating account subject to the bank's FX desk and foreign-exchange declarations. For supplier payments, SWIFT MT103 is the appropriate single-currency wire clearing rail; for documentary trade, a commercial letter of credit opened by the Colombian bank through MT700 and subsequently settled via MT103/MT202 is preferred. All outbound payments for imported goods or services must be supported by the relevant DIAN import declaration, commercial invoice, service contract, license agreement, or similar underlying transaction documentation, and the local bank will complete a Declaración de Cambio by import classification at the time the client purchases FX. Tournament-winning disbursements to foreign players should be made through the same regulated banking channel, as direct offshore payment from Stripe/PayPal balances to third-party prize recipients may inflate the underwriting risk of the platform and create complicated FX-compliance records. For material outbound treasury disbursements, the S.A.S. should maintain a centralized beneficiary-beneficiary payment matrix and submit the bank instructions in advance to avoid fragmented ad-hoc wires.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD spot transactions through authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediaries
COP/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in COP or USD
Cross-currency swaps between COP and USD
European-style USD/COP currency options negotiated OTC with a registered financial institution
Exchange-traded USD/COP futures or standardized FX contracts permitted by the Colombian financial supervisor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) coordinated with RUES and DIAN
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a statutory surcharge (up to 9.2% of the assessed renewal fee), potential suspension of the merchant registration, and failure to renew for two consecutive years can lead to administrative cancellation of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Financial Statements Approved by Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting; subsequently filed with the Chamber of Commerce (RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end (31 December), generally by 31 March if no extension is adopted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing of the approved financial statements with the Chamber of Commerce may result in monetary fines, restrictions on obtaining certificates of incorporation good standing, and in repeated non-compliance, deregistration procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax and Complementaries Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Departamento de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ends 31 December; filing deadline established by DIAN resolution based on NIT last digit, typically between 15 and 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to 5% of the tax assessed or up to 1% of gross income, plus late payment interest and inflation adjustment; repeated failure or false declarations may lead to DIAN enforcement actions, asset seizure, and administrative sanctions, though not direct commercial strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Colombian S.A.S. must appoint a statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) when any of the following is met: (i) gross assets or gross revenues in the previous fiscal year exceed 5,000 UVT (Colombian Tax Value Unit); (ii) shareholders representing no less than 20% of the capital request the appointment via court-recognized petition; (iii) the company is a public-interest entity or is subject to special legal regimes. In the absence of such criteria, an external audit is generally voluntary, but must comply with effective assurance standards where elected.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Colombia (International Financial Reporting Standards, full version for open entities; IFRS for SMEs for smaller S.A.S. entities that qualify as non-public interest companies with assets or revenues within the local thresholds, per Law 1314/2009 and CTCP guidelines)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must annually report and confirm its Beneficiario Final (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) to the Chamber of Commerce/RUES and DIAN as part of the commercial registry renewal process, no later than 31 March. This includes any natural person owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, at least 5% of shares, votes, or economic rights, or benefiting from 3% or more of profits, or exercising significant control via other mechanisms. Ownership transfers must be reflected in the shareholder registry and the annual confirmation submission.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Socios y Representantes)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea y de Junta Directiva)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300 - 900 (market range for registered office in major cities like Bogotá or Medellín, excluding virtual office services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,200 - 3,500 (certified independent audit fee range for a small-to-mid-size S.A.S. engaged in software/e-commerce, subject to complexity and entity scope)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% general corporate income tax (CIT) applicable to Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) for fiscal tax periods from 2023 onward per Law 2277 of 2022.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Orange Economy preferential CIT exemption: software development, digital content, and esports-related creative industries may benefit from a ten-year 0% CIT exemption on qualifying revenues under Law 1955 of 2019 and Law 2068 of 2020, subject to DIAN registration, annual certification, and strict compliance; ordinary non-qualifying income remains taxed at 35%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 100 (Cédula General) — annual corporate income tax and complementary tax return; filed electronically through the DIAN electronic filing system or an authorized e-DIAN software provider.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal period ended on 31 December; combined with quarterly advance payments (anticipos) and the separate transfer-pricing informative return (Form 120).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory due date falls between 9 April and 13 May of the following tax year, determined by the penultimate digit of the taxpayer's NIT (Tax ID), as published by DIAN each year; no general extensions are granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income including esports tournament fees, matchmaking subscription revenue, sponsorship income, and digital platform commissions before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Colombian S.A.S. owned by non-residents, report all Colombian-sourced and export-derived gross revenues at market exchange rates; do not consolidate foreign parent revenues on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt and excluded income such as the Orange Economy software content revenues qualifying for the 10-year CIT benefit or treaty-protected items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if the SAS has registered the creative activity with the Ministry of Culture and stored proof of the DIAN exemption certificate; non-resident shareholders must not assume that foreign ownership automatically preserves this exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legitimate operating costs and deductions, including cloud hosting, prize payouts to players, marketing, operational staff, rent, and transfer-pricing-compliant related-party charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must document all cross-border service/royalty payments with transfer-pricing files and backup invoices from the foreign recipient; otherwise deductions will be disallowed and penalized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income after applying prior-year loss carryforwards (maximum 12 years) and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned S.A.S., ensure the annual CNU/DSM (Beneficiary Registry) and SAGRI tax information of the ultimate shareholder is aligned with this taxable base; mismatches trigger automatic DIAN audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT liability computed at the 35% headline rate (or effective Orange Economy rate) after tax-credit reductions and non-deductible items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder must not pay this liability itself; corporate level taxation is independent from dividend WHT at the repatriation stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits claimed for prepaid quarterly tax advances and withholding taxes withheld by payment gateways or sponsors from remittances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that Stripe, PayPal, or ecommerce rails actually withheld any Colombian tax at source; if not, no withholding credit may be recognized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or credit carryforward after offsetting all credits and payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must sign the 'Declaraciones del revisor fiscal' if applicable and obtain certification before repatriating profits to avoid dividend unavailability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or omission of the Form 100 triggers a fine of 5% for each month or fraction of lateness on the tax due, capped at 100% of such tax; if no tax is due, a fine between 10 and 1,000 UVT (2024 UVT = COP 47,024) is imposed. Daily interest accrues at the DIAN central bank rate, and an inexact declaration may face a penalty of up to 200% of the understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends distributed to foreign shareholders: 5% withholding on the portion representing profits already subject to CIT; 35% withholding on profits that were exempt such as some Orange Economy earnings; effective combined CIT+WHT on ordinary operating profits is 38.75%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a double tax agreement (DTA) and reduce dividend WHT, the foreign shareholder must provide the Colombian paying S.A.S. with an official Tax Residency Certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal, CRF) from the shareholder's own tax authority, a written Beneficial Ownership declaration and documentary evidence that the shareholder has no permanent establishment in Colombia. The CRF must cover the exact fiscal period of the dividend distribution and be sent to DIAN via the 'Form 100', 'Form 110', and the e-file 'Trámite de solicitud de reducción de retención' before the next remittance; without these the statutory rate applies.

cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht.statutory_and_treaty_rates_for_IP_royalt: Statutory WHT on non-resident royalties (software, platform IP, esports technology rights) is 15%; statutory WHT on interest and financial expenses to foreign lenders is 15%. Under the Colombia-US DTA and several other DTAs, royalties may be reduced to 10% (or 0% for copyright royalties) and interest to 0%–10% if the recipient is the beneficial owner. To obtain treaty rates, the local payer must submit the CRF and a Form 30 'Devolución/Compensación' for excess withholding if already withheld at 15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Transfer pricing Local File and Master File are mandatory when the taxpayer's gross income exceeds COP 4,232 million (90,000 UVT in 2024) or gross assets exceed COP 9,405 million (200,000 UVT in 2024), and related-party transactions exceed COP 1,270 million (27,000 UVT in 2024). The separate TP Informative Return (Form 120) is due annually under those thresholds, with deviations in November of the following year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not maintain a dedicated Economic Substance Regulation statutory act, but the General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 658-bis E.T.) allows DIAN to disregard a S.A.S. as fiscally transparent or as an abusive shell if it lacks real premises, employees, decision-making activity, and actual it-platform infrastructure in Colombia. For an esports platform, substance evidence must include server logs, developer payroll, Colombian bank accounts, tournament prize-flow contracts, and meeting minutes of the board of directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion / hidden digital revenues
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to declare revenue received through Stripe/PayPal, virtual wallets, crypto, or tournament entry fees; using undisclosed offshore accounts to collect platform income; or inflating costs with invoices from shell companies that provide no real esports-related services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority re-determines taxable income and imposes a deficiency penalty of up to 200% of the evaded CIT (Article 779 E.T.); criminal prosecution under Article 434-A of the Colombian Criminal Code (evasión fiscal) carries imprisonment of 48 to 108 months and fines equal to 100%–200% of the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives of the S.A.S. are jointly liable for the evaded tax and interest, and in criminal tax cases may receive travel bans issued by DIAN, asset embargoes, personal restitution orders, and terms of imprisonment of up to nine years if their tax noncompliance is deemed intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / abusive economic substance structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Colombian S.A.S. solely as a booking and distribution vehicle for tournament prize money while all real decision-making and technological activity occurs abroad; having no Colombian employees, office space, bank account, or local server operation for software / esports services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN rejects the corporate structure under Article 658-bis (abuso de la naturaleza jurídica), disallows deductible expenses, recasts revenue at the level of the real foreign owner, denies Orange Economy exemptions, and levies a general tax fine of 5%–200% of the adjusted CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under Law 222 of 1995 when the S.A.S. is used for fraudulent, abusive, tax-avoidance purposes; directors can be personally ordered to pay the full tax deficiency, face a ban on international travel until the debt is secured, and be prosecuted for document falsification when signatures on annual returns are deemed materially inaccurate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing noncompliance for related party cross-border fee flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into excessive royalty, management, or software license agreements with a foreign related party (e.g., a parent company in Mexico or USA) that exceed the arm's length standard; failing to prepare and file the Local File/Master File and TP Informative Return (Form 120) on time.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN adjusts the price to the arm's length value and charges a TP penalty of up to 20% on the resulting CIT adjustment, plus late-filing fines of 5% per month up to 200% of unpaid tax and interest; failure to file Form 120 carries an additional fine of 10–15,000 UVT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incorrect TP declarations face personal liability for the adjustment and penalized tax; in aggravated cases, they may be named in criminal charges of 'falsedad en documento privado' with imprisonment of up to six years and be subject to anti-money-laundering investigation under the predicate offense of tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / terrorism funding / unauthorized payment rails around tournament prize payouts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unlicensed digital remitters, anonymous prepaid cards, or mixing corporate tournament prize flow with director personal PayPal/Stripe accounts; failing to verify sanctioned individuals or politically exposed persons; paying prizes without AML filtering through the Corporate Beneficial Owner Registry (CUES/CNU/SAGRI).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Article 323 of the Colombian Criminal Code (lavado de activos) is punishable by 9 to 20 years of imprisonment and fines of up to 50,000 statutory minimum monthly wages; the Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF) may freeze accounts, and the S.A.S. may lose its passport-style banking license privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Chairman/CEO are treated as 'personas expuestas políticamente' where control failures appear; they may receive a travel ban, company asset seizure, and personal fines up to 20,000 SMMLV, in addition to criminal imprisonment in connection with predicate crimes of tax evasion or illicit enrichment through the platform.
